Scope Gate.decided_by: omn-business-analyst subagent acfda7bd565a5f491, recorded by session operator for vuhoangcao
Scope Gate.rationale: Approve with conditions. Drift claims in SCOPE-2026-0013 verified against both files: docs/USER-GUIDE.md line 538 carries '5b. Branch naming templates' with token reference, normalization rules and migration notes, and docs/user-guide.html has no counterpart; gate-ownership material sits before '5c' in the source (line 818) but at the end of the driving-a-run chapter in the published page (line 901). Eight in-scope items map one-to-one onto the request's three deliverables plus its affordance-preservation sentence; nothing in the request is uncovered. D-002 and D-004 are correct and forced by the input rather than chosen: the literal 'no content in exactly one file' criterion is unsatisfiable for a markup form and contradicts the same request's preserve-the-affordances instruction, and once the published form is derived, preserving its order would mean reordering the source, which X-003 excludes. Six findings, none blocking: four under-specifications that would leave an implementer guessing (D-002 authored-vs-derived line undefined; A-013 'raw markup line' not reproducibly countable; A-008's nine chapter anchors plus six in-chapter anchors are hand-chosen slugs not derivable from headings, a tension with S-007/A-013 the scope never records; S-008/A-014 target an instruction absent from contributor prose) and two minor (A-006 resolution list has no named home; D-004's visible reordering is unsignalled to readers). FIVE CONDITIONS bind downstream phases: (1) record the authored-vs-derived test using the Q-002 rule before implementation, listing every derived-classified string in the A-006 list with its classification rather than dropping it silently; (2) define 'raw markup line' as a rule an independent reviewer can apply, and record that A-008 (must-have) governs over A-013 where they conflict, A-013 being reported not enforced; (3) architect must answer anchor notation explicitly, treating the fifteen identifiers as a fixed set carried through regeneration; (4) restate A-014 against the concrete targets from the Q-001 answer, recording that committed change proposals and run evidence are out of its reach; (5) persist the A-006 resolution list as a named artifact of the implementation phase. Q-001 answered: no hand-synchronisation instruction exists in contributor prose. README.md mentions the guide once (line 134) with no such instruction; the only live statement is the docstring of tests/test_ci_workflow.py line 190, 'the HTML handbook is hand-synced with the markdown guide'. S-008 resolves to updating that docstring and adding the regeneration instruction to README.md and the handbook's own maintenance material. Q-002 answered by rule, not by owner: HTML-only wording stating a fact (masthead kicker; footer tool version, command-reference pointer, source statement) is authored content and merges into the source; HTML-only strings that only label or route within the page (navigation link text, chapter eyebrows) are derived presentation, regenerated from the heading they point at, divergent wording dropped; every drop recorded in the A-006 list; genuinely ambiguous items escalate to omn-product-owner, not the implementer. The footer's source statement folds into the S-005 banner rather than merging twice.

Planning Gate.decided_by: omn-tech-lead subagent abe206986eea387d2, recorded by session operator for vuhoangcao
Planning Gate.rationale: Approve with conditions. Decomposition is faithful to the approved boundary: all eight in-scope items and the five Scope Gate conditions are covered by named tasks, nothing outside the seven exclusions is planned, and the eight-wave order is executable - all 38 dependency edges run from a strictly lower wave to a strictly higher one, so the graph is acyclic and no wave consumes what a later wave produces. Sequencing on the highest-impact risk is right in principle (T-003 fixes the four determinism decisions in wave 3 before T-002 builds the renderer in wave 4) but insufficient in practice, because the only cross-platform proof T-004 lands in wave 7, after five tasks have been built on an unproven assumption. Six findings, none blocking. (1) MAJOR: assumption A-002 is true for a STEP and false for a JOB - tests/test_ci_workflow.py::test_job_topology_and_stable_names asserts the job set equals exactly {discover, tests, verifier-ubuntu, verifier-windows, verifiers-ubuntu-ok, verifiers-windows-ok}, so a new job breaks the suite; the matrix does cover both platforms via the tests job, so an added step there is accepted without restructuring. R-006 overstates an uncertainty that is in fact a precise constraint. Operator independently confirmed the assertion at tests/test_ci_workflow.py lines 62-74. (2) MAJOR: failing is not blocking - only tests-ubuntu is required from day one; tests-windows and both verifiers-*-ok names are advisory until the flip. A drift check placed as a discovered verify_*.py under the framework runtime directory would run and go red WITHOUT stopping a merge, defeating the scope's success measure S-002/A-003. T-016 records no check-name constraint. (3) MAJOR: scope acceptance criterion A-002 (a direct edit to the published file does not survive regeneration) has no executing task - T-002 proves repeat-identity, T-004 platform-identity, T-019 the CI fail/pass pair, but no task performs the discard demonstration. (4) MAJOR: R-003 mitigation validates too late - decisions precede the build but proof arrives four waves later, after T-002, T-005, T-015, T-016, T-017; line-ending divergence on the windows leg is closer to likely than medium. (5) MAJOR: R-002 has a LIVE instance - pyyaml appears in docs/user-guide.html (dependency-footprint paragraph, line 246, and the V-IMPORT troubleshooting row, line 989) and nowhere in docs/USER-GUIDE.md, while tests/test_omn_agent.py line 775 asserts it in the published file. Operator independently confirmed. The four stable check names and verify.yml are present in both and are safe. (6) MINOR: A-008 confirmed - both legs provision python identically and existing steps use byte-identical run strings across platforms, so one 'python <path>' command line serves both provided it uses no shell-specific quoting, no && and no backslash paths. Q-003 DECIDED AS A RULE: a string asserted by a committed test is non-droppable and the assertion governs. Where the authored-content test would drop an item whose text an existing test asserts, the implementer records the resolution as MERGED INTO THE SOURCE - not dropped, not escalated - so the regenerated published file still carries it.
